method_md:
# hydraulicnetwork.html — method specification for an independent reference

Scope: the steady-state network solve of `hydraulicnetwork.html` (manifest revision
`2026-10-15.hydraulicnetwork-3`; the changes from `2026-09-11.report-profile-1` are listed in
section 12), as documented by the page's Learn text, its model footer, the
calculation-record equations and the manifest limitations. Where those texts are silent, the law
the page code applies is stated here as a plain equation and marked **[code]**. Nothing in this
file is a result; `cases.json` holds inputs and graded keys only.

The ensemble sweeps (pump/system curve, N-1, Monte-Carlo, load profile) and auto-balance are out
of scope.

## 1. Units and constants

| Quantity | Unit in the document | SI used in the laws |
|---|---|---|
| node elevation `z` | m | m |
| node demand `demand` | m³/h (positive = withdrawn from the network) | ÷ 3600 → m³/s |
| fixed-node pressure `p` | kPa, gauge | × 1000 → Pa |
| pipe length `L` | m | m |
| pipe diameter `D`, roughness `eps` | mm | ÷ 1000 → m |
| pump `H0`, `Hrated` | m | m |
| pump `Qrated` | m³/h | ÷ 3600 → m³/s |
| pump `speed`, valve `opening`, `loadFactor`, `speedFactor` | % | ÷ 100 |
| valve `Kv` | m³/h per √bar | — |
| heat exchanger `Qdesign` | m³/h | ÷ 3600 → m³/s |
| heat exchanger `dpDesign` | kPa | × 1000 → Pa |
| density `rho` | kg/m³ | kg/m³ |
| kinematic viscosity `nu` | m²/s | m²/s |

g = 9.80665 m/s² **[code]** (standard gravity). Flows inside the laws are m³/s unless a law says
m³/h.

## 2. Input document (what `cases.json` → `case.input` contains)

A JSON object, imported through the page's "Open network JSON" file input:

```
{
  "schema":   "tools.petrov.re/hydraulic-network/v2",   // v1 also accepted; absent accepted
  "fluid":    { "rho": <kg/m3>, "nu": <m2/s> },
  "analysis": { "loadFactor": <%>, "speedFactor": <%> },
  "nodes":    [ { "id", "name", "x", "y", "z", "demand", "fixed", "p" }, ... ],
  "edges":    [ { "id", "name", "type", "a", "b", ...type fields }, ... ]
}
```

Node fields: `id` (string, starts with a letter, then letters/digits/`_.:-`, ≤ 64 chars), `name`
(display only), `x`, `y` (drawing coordinates, no physics; must lie in 0…1000 × 0…620), `z`,
`demand`, `fixed` (boolean), `p` (used only when `fixed` is true).

Edge fields common to all types: `id` (same pattern as nodes), `name`, `type` ∈ {`pipe`, `pump`,
`valve`, `hx`}, `a` (start node id), `b` (end node id). The arrow a → b is the positive flow
direction.

| type | fields |
|---|---|
| `pipe` | `L`, `D`, `eps`, `K` (sum of minor-loss coefficients) |
| `pump` | `H0` (shutoff head), `Qrated`, `Hrated`, `speed` (local speed, %) |
| `valve` | `Kv` (rated), `opening` (%), `law` ∈ {`linear`, `equal`}, `target` (m³/h, used only by auto-balance — no effect on a solve) |
| `hx` | `Qdesign`, `dpDesign`, `n` |

Defaults applied by the importer when a field is absent **[code]** (every case supplies every
field, so these matter only for completeness): node `z` 0, `demand` 0, `fixed` false, `p` 0; pipe
L 20, D 50, eps 0.045, K 0; pump H0 18, Qrated 12, Hrated 12, speed 100; valve Kv 10, opening 100,
law `linear`, target 0; hx Qdesign 10, dpDesign 25, n 2; fluid rho 998, nu 1.004e-6; loadFactor
100, speedFactor 100.

**Analysis factors on import:** `loadFactor` and `speedFactor` are applied exactly as written
(any finite value inside the ranges of section 8, e.g. 87.6 % or 0.5 %); there is no rounding.

Case-level fields in `cases.json` that are not part of the document: `input_text` (malformed_json
only: the exact bytes to import; `input` is null), `refusal` (true when the case exists to test a
refusal), `grid` (Swamee–Jain cases: the nominal Re and ε/D each pipe was generated from — the
stored demand, D, eps and nu are authoritative), `sequence` (throttling cases: ordered member of a
monotonicity sequence), `generator` (random meshes: provenance only, the stored network is
authoritative), `note`.

## 3. Fluid

Density ρ and kinematic viscosity ν are constants for the whole network (no temperature
dependence). Specific gravity used by the valve law: SG = ρ / 1000 **[code]** (the reference
density is exactly 1000 kg/m³).

## 4. Unknowns, equations and boundary conditions

Unknowns: the volumetric flow q_e of every edge (m³/s, positive a → b) and the pressure head h_n
of every free (non-fixed) node (m).

Total head (hydraulic grade line) of a node: H_n = h_n + z_n. Velocity head is excluded
everywhere.

Fixed-pressure node: h_n = p_n·1000 / (ρ g); its elevation still enters H_n. Every connected
component of the graph must contain at least one fixed node; a closed circuit needs one
arbitrary reference.

Effective demand: d_n = demand_n · (loadFactor/100) / 3600 (m³/s). The load factor scales every
nodal demand (fixed or free) and nothing else.

Continuity at every free node n:

  Σ_{e: b_e = n} q_e − Σ_{e: a_e = n} q_e − d_n = 0

Energy along every edge e (all component types):

  H_{a_e} − H_{b_e} + H_pump,e(q_e) − h_loss,e(q_e) = 0

where H_pump = 0 for passive components and h_loss = 0 for pumps. All passive losses are odd in
q: h_loss(q) = sign(q)·|h_loss|(|q|), and h_loss(0) = 0.

Boundary exchange of a fixed node n (reported, not imposed) **[code]**:

  B_n = d_n + Σ_{e: a_e = n} q_e − Σ_{e: b_e = n} q_e   (positive = flow entering the network there)

Multiple edges between the same pair of nodes are allowed (parallel components).

## 5. Component laws

### 5.1 Pipe (Darcy–Weisbach)

A = π D²/4, v = |q|/A, Re = v D / ν, r = eps / D (eps and D in the same unit)

|h_loss| = (f L / D + K) · v² / (2 g)

K multiplies the pipe's own velocity head.

Darcy friction factor f(Re, r):

- Re = 0 (no flow): f = 0 **[code]**, loss 0.
- Re ≤ 2000: f = 64 / Re (Hagen–Poiseuille).
- Re ≥ 4000: Swamee–Jain, f_SJ = 0.25 / [log₁₀( r/3.7 + 5.74 / Re^0.9 )]².
- 2000 < Re < 4000: smoothstep blend **[code for the exact form; the Learn text says
  "smoothstep blend"]**: t = (Re − 2000)/2000, s = t²(3 − 2t),
  f = (1 − s)·64/Re + s·f_SJ(Re, r).

Published validity of Swamee–Jain (Swamee & Jain 1976): 1e-6 ≤ ε/D ≤ 1e-2 and
5e3 ≤ Re ≤ 1e8; the page states it differs from the Colebrook–White root by up to about 3 % in f
inside that box. The page uses f_SJ unchanged outside the box (no clipping) and warns
(section 9).

### 5.2 Valve (metric Kv)

o = clamp(opening/100, 0.001, 1) **[code; the clamp is inactive because openings below 0.1 %
are refused, section 8]**

Kv_eff = Kv · o (law `linear`); Kv_eff = Kv · 50^(o − 1) (law `equal`, equal percentage with
rangeability 50).

Δp[bar] = SG · (|q|·3600 / Kv_eff)², i.e. Δp[Pa] = 1e5 · SG · (Q[m³/h] / Kv_eff)²,
|h_loss| = Δp[Pa] / (ρ g).

### 5.3 Heat exchanger (hydraulic resistance only)

|h_loss| = (dpDesign·1000 / (ρ g)) · (|q| / (Qdesign/3600))^n,  1 ≤ n ≤ 3.

No thermal model.

### 5.4 Pump (two-point quadratic, affinity law)

s = (speed/100) · (speedFactor/100)
a = (H0 − Hrated) / (Qrated/3600)²   (m per (m³/s)²)
H_pump(q) = H0 · s² − a · q · |q|

The rated point lies on the s = 1 curve; the affinity law scales the shutoff head by s² and
leaves the quadratic coefficient unchanged (equivalently H(Q, s) = s² H(Q/s, 1)). For q < 0 the
same expression is used (H0 s² + a q²): reverse flow is an extrapolation, not a check valve.
Zero-head runout: q_runout = √(H0 s² / a). A pump has no separate loss term.

## 6. Solution and convergence (how close the page's numbers are to the exact root)

The page solves all unknowns simultaneously by damped Newton on scaled residuals with a
central-difference Jacobian and dense Gauss–Jordan elimination with partial pivoting. It stops when
the infinity norm of the scaled residual vector is ≤ 2e-9, or after 60 iterations. Scaling
**[code]**: continuity residuals are divided by q_scale, energy residuals by h_scale, where

- h_scale = max(5, |fixed-node pressure heads|, |all z|, |H0 s²| of every pump) in m;
- q_scale = max(1e-5, largest of |d_n| and |Qrated·s/3600| over pumps) in m³/s; if that largest
  value is ≤ 1e-9 (no demand and no pump), q_scale = max(1e-5, an estimate of the largest single-edge
  flow that the fixed-head span would drive).

So an energy residual of up to 2e-9·h_scale m and a continuity residual of up to 2e-9·q_scale
m³/s are acceptable to the page. Post-processing **[code]**: a passive edge whose two end nodes are
both fixed and whose end HGLs differ by less than 1e-12 m is assigned q = 0 exactly.

Outcomes: converged (scaled residual ≤ 2e-9); stopped at the 60-iteration cap with scaled residual
in (2e-9, 2e-6] → reported as a result flagged unconverged (`solved_capped`); scaled residual >
2e-6 after the cap → refused (`no_convergence`). A singular Jacobian, a failed line search or a
non-finite residual also refuse the solve.

## 7. Graded output keys (units as in `case.graded`)

| key | definition |
|---|---|
| `outcome` | `solved`, `solved_capped`, `refused_at_import`, `refused_at_solve` |
| `message_kind` | kind of the refusal message (section 9); `none` when solved |
| `warnings` | ordered list of `{kind, components[]}` (section 9); components are edge ids |
| `flow_<e>` | q_e · 3600, m³/h, signed (positive a → b) |
| `head_loss_<e>` | signed h_loss,e(q_e), m (passive edges) |
| `dp_loss_<e>` | ρ g · head_loss_e / 1000, kPa (valves) |
| `pump_head_<e>` | H_pump,e(q_e), m |
| `head_across_<e>` | H_{b_e} − H_{a_e}, m (pumps) |
| `pressure_<n>` | gauge pressure h_n ρ g / 1000, kPa (fixed nodes: the prescribed value) |
| `hgl_<n>` | H_n = h_n + z_n, m |
| `boundary_<n>` | B_n · 3600, m³/h (fixed nodes) |
| `velocity_<e>`, `Re_<e>`, `f_<e>` | pipe v (m/s), Re (−), Darcy f (−) at the solved flow |
| `node_count_after_import`, `edge_count_after_import` | element counts held after import (no silent truncation) |
| `notification_kind` | style of the notification the import raises: `ok` (accepted), `err` (refused); see section 8 |

Throttling sequence (`group: monotone_throttling`): in addition to the per-case keys, across the
four cases ordered by decreasing opening, flow_E4 and flow_E1 are graded for strict decrease and
flow_E5 for strict increase.

## 8. Refusal triggers and the stage at which they act **[code; the Learn text says only that the
importer "validates every field before it touches the canvas"]**

Import stage (the document is rejected, the previously loaded network stays on the canvas and an
error-style notification, kind `err`, shows the message; an accepted import raises a success-style
notification, kind `ok`, "Network loaded"). Checked in this order; the first failing check is
reported:

1. file larger than 5 MB → `too_large`
2. not parseable as JSON → `invalid_json`
3. not an object, or `nodes`/`edges` not arrays → `invalid_document`
4. `schema` present and not `tools.petrov.re/hydraulic-network/v1` or `…/v2` → `unsupported_schema`
5. a numeric field present but not finite → "<field> must be finite"; `fixed` present but not boolean
6. more than 1000 nodes or 3000 edges; ρ ≤ 0; ν ≤ 0; load factor outside 0–150 %; speed factor
   outside 40–120 % (`load_factor_range`, `speed_factor_range`)
7. per node, in order: id pattern (`invalid_id`), duplicate id (`duplicate_node_id`), name > 200
   chars, non-finite x/y/z/demand/p, coordinates outside the canvas (`coordinates`)
8. per edge, in order: id pattern, duplicate edge id (`duplicate_edge_id`), name length, endpoint
   not an existing node (`invalid_endpoint`), a = b (`self_loop`), unknown type, then type checks:
   - pipe: L ≤ 0 or D ≤ 0 (`pipe_geometry`); eps < 0 or K < 0 (`pipe_roughness_or_K`)
   - valve: Kv ≤ 0 (`valve_kv`); opening < 0.1 or > 100 (`valve_opening_out_of_range`); target < 0;
     law not `linear`/`equal` (`valve_law`)
   - hx: Qdesign ≤ 0, dpDesign ≤ 0, n outside [1, 3] (`hx_parameters`)
   - pump: H0 ≤ 0, Qrated ≤ 0 or Hrated < 0 (`pump_parameters`); Hrated ≥ H0
     (`pump_rated_not_below_shutoff`); speed outside 1–150 % (`pump_speed`)

Solve stage (the document imported; pressing Solve refuses):

1. fewer than 2 nodes or no edge (`too_few_elements`)
2. a node with no edge (`isolated_node`)
3. edges + free nodes > 600 (`unknown_limit`) — the page's declared limit of 600 nonlinear unknowns
4. a connected component without a fixed node (`no_pressure_reference`)
5. solver failures of section 6 (`singular_jacobian`, `divergence`, `no_convergence`)

## 9. Warnings after a solve (the solve succeeds)

Listed in this order **[code]**:

Tie rule: the Re used for classification is the solved Re, except that a solved Re within a
relative 1e-7 of 2000, 4000, 5e3 or 1e8 is taken as that threshold value; likewise ε/D within a
relative 1e-7 of 1e-6 or 1e-2 is taken as the bound. The window is wider than the Re error the
stopping rule of section 6 can leave on a pipe (up to about 4e-8 relative) and narrower than the
1e-6 offsets of case `sj_re_threshold_ties`. With that value:

1. `transition_blend` — pipes with 2000 < Re < 4000 (edge order). Re = 2000 is laminar and not
   listed.
2. `outside_swamee_jain_range` — pipes with Re ≥ 4000 and (Re < 5e3 or Re > 1e8 or ε/D < 1e-6 or
   ε/D > 1e-2) (edge order). A pipe on Re = 4000 is listed here (4000 < 5e3) and not under 1; the
   box is closed, so Re = 5e3, Re = 1e8, ε/D = 1e-6 and ε/D = 1e-2 are inside. ε = 0 (ε/D = 0) is
   outside. A pipe already listed under 1 is not listed here. Laminar pipes are never listed.

The tie rule affects only the warning lists: the friction law of section 5.1 uses the solved Re
unchanged (f is continuous at 2000 and 4000).
3. per pump in edge order: `pump_reverse_flow` if q < 0; `pump_beyond_runout` if
   q > 1.001 · q_runout.

## 10. Ambiguities and points a reference must decide

- **A1 Lower ε/D bound.** Resolved in revision 2026-10-15: ε/D < 1e-6, including ε = 0, is
  warned (section 9).
- **A2 Non-integer analysis factors.** Resolved in revision 2026-10-15: applied as written
  (section 2).
- **A3 Regime boundaries.** Resolved in revision 2026-10-15 by the tie rule of section 9. A pipe
  generated on a threshold is classified at the threshold whatever side round-off puts its solved
  Re; a pipe 1e-6 relative away from a threshold (case `sj_re_threshold_ties`) is classified by its
  side.
- **A4 Opening clamp.** The 0.001 floor in the Kv law is unreachable through import (openings
  < 0.1 % refused); 0.1 % gives o = 0.001 exactly either way.
- **A5 Specific gravity** is ρ/1000, not ρ/ρ_water(T).
- **A6 Pump reverse flow and runout** are extrapolations of the same parabola (section 5.4); they
  are warned, not modelled differently.
- **A7 Velocity head** is excluded from H; the minor-loss K uses the pipe's own velocity; there is
  no junction loss.
- **A8 Demand at a fixed node** does not enter any equation except its boundary exchange B_n.
- **A9 Convergence floor.** Page values are roots only to the scaled-residual gate of section 6; a
  reference tolerance must not be tighter than what that gate allows for the case's h_scale and
  q_scale.
- **A10 Zero-flow snap** between two fixed nodes of equal HGL (section 6).
- **A11 Warnings name components by `name`**; the graded `warnings` list uses edge ids (the driver
  maps names back; in every case names are unique).
- **A12 Swamee–Jain constants** are used exactly as printed (0.25, 3.7, 5.74, 0.9, log₁₀); no
  Colebrook iteration.

## 11. Literature (as cited by the previous benchmark artifact)

- P.K. Swamee & A.K. Jain, Explicit equations for pipe-flow problems, ASCE J. Hydraulics Div.
  102(5) (1976) 657–664 — f = 0.25/[log₁₀(ε/(3.7 D) + 5.74/Re^0.9)]², stated for
  1e-6 ≤ ε/D ≤ 1e-2 and 5e3 ≤ Re ≤ 1e8.
- C.F. Colebrook, J. Inst. Civ. Eng. 11 (1939) 133–156 — only to quantify Swamee–Jain scatter.
- Hagen–Poiseuille laminar closed form f = 64/Re.
- H. Cross, Analysis of Flow in Networks of Conduits or Conductors, Univ. of Illinois Eng. Exp.
  Station Bulletin 286 (1936) — loop-correction method (a possible independent solver).
- IEC 60534-2-1 / metric Kv definition: Q[m³/h] = Kv √(Δp[bar]/SG).
- Affinity law H ∝ n² for the two-point quadratic pump curve.

The heat-exchanger power law, the two-point pump parabola and the 2000–4000 smoothstep blend are
the page's own declared models, not external standards.

## 12. Revision 2026-10-15 (page `2026-10-15.hydraulicnetwork-3`)

| id | change | clauses | cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Analysis factors are applied as written; the integer-percent rounding on import is removed. Range checks unchanged. | §2 "Analysis factors on import", §10 A2 | changed: `partial_load_non_integer`; new: `partial_load_62_5`, `partial_load_0_5`, `pump_speed_factor_97_5`, `pump_speed_factor_87_6`, `load_factor_above_range`, `speed_factor_below_range` |
| R2 | The range warning also lists ε/D < 1e-6 (including ε = 0); the warning text states the box as 5e3≤Re≤1e8, 1e-6≤ε/D≤1e-2. | §9 item 2, §10 A1 | changed: `sj_laminar_blend_range` (S16, S17); new: `sj_eps_bounds` |

expected.author_note: Independent reference for hydraulicnetwork.html (method.md, revision 2026-10-15.hydraulicnetwork-3, spec changes R1-R4 applied; previous issue 2026-10-11 kept as blind/expected_rev2026-10-11.json). Built only from blind/cases.json, blind/method.md, the cited literature and engineering knowledge. Method A (expected values): node-head Newton posed as convex content minimisation (each component law inverted to q(dH); exact line search on the monotone directional derivative; free heads converged until the continuity residual is <= 1e-14 of the flow scale). Method B (cross-check): mixed (q,H) Newton in Todini-Pilati global-gradient form with analytic derivatives. Method C (cross-check where topology allows): explicit per-edge inversion between fixed heads, continuity-only flows on trees, nested scalar Brent roots for series/parallel/pump lines. Numbers are double precision; Swamee-Jain and every other law exactly as written in method.md. Script: blind/reference.py.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A1 lower eps/D bound of the Swamee-Jain box (resolved by R2)
method_decisions.decision: Per method.md rev 2026-10-15: a turbulent pipe (Re >= 4000) with eps/D < 1e-6, including eps = 0, is warned outside_swamee_jain_range; eps/D = 1e-6 itself is inside.
method_decisions.why: Follows the revised section 9. concern (kept, now about the warning rather than the page text): below eps/D = 1e-6 Swamee-Jain tends to its smooth-pipe limit and stays within 0.3 % of Colebrook here (crosscheck.swamee_jain_vs_colebrook: sj_eps_bounds S1/S2, sj_laminar_blend_range S16/S17), better than inside the box near eps/D = 1e-2 (up to 2.8 %). The warning on smooth pipes therefore flags no loss of accuracy; it is a statement about the fitted range only.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A2 non-integer analysis factors (resolved by R1)
method_decisions.decision: Per method.md rev 2026-10-15: loadFactor and speedFactor applied exactly as written (87.6 %, 62.5 %, 0.5 %, 97.5 %, 87.6 % speed). The 2026-10-11 rounding to 88 % is reverted.
method_decisions.why: The factor is a continuous multiplier of demand (and of pump speed through the affinity law); nothing in hydraulics quantises it. The earlier concern about silent rounding is closed by R1.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A3 regime boundaries (resolved by R4 tie rule)
method_decisions.decision: Warnings classify on the solved Re, taken as the threshold when within 1e-7 relative of 2000, 4000, 5e3 or 1e8 (eps/D likewise at 1e-6 and 1e-2). Re = 2000 laminar (not listed), Re = 4000 Swamee-Jain branch (listed outside the box, 4000 < 5e3), Re = 5e3, 1e8, eps/D = 1e-6, 1e-2 inside the closed box. The friction factor uses the solved Re unchanged. On tree cases the Re fed to the rule is evaluated in rational arithmetic of the stored demands (agrees with the float Re of the solved flow to ~1e-15).
method_decisions.why: Follows the revised section 9. The 1e-7 window covers the worst-case Re error the page stopping rule (2e-9 on scaled residuals, propagated through |J^-1|) allows on every tie pipe: 2e-9 to 4e-8 relative (sj_grid_re_5e3_1e5 S1-S5 4e-8, sj_laminar_blend_range S6 1e-8 / S12 5e-9, sj_re_threshold_ties S2/S5/S8 2e-9 to 5e-9, sj_grid_re_1e6_1e8 S11-S15 2e-9), and is 10x narrower than the 1e-6 offsets of sj_re_threshold_ties, which are classified by their side. crosscheck.warning_threshold_proximity is absent in every case, so no expected warning depends on how deeply the page converges. The earlier residual concern (window narrower than the gate) is closed.

method_decisions.decision: refused_at_import -> err; any accepted import (solved, or refused later at solve) -> ok.
method_decisions.why: Per method.md sections 7-8 and cases.json spec_changes R3, which agree (ok/err only).

method_decisions.decision: o = opening/100 with the 0.001 floor; 0.1 % gives o = 0.001 (Kv_eff = Kv/1000 linear, Kv x 50^-0.999 equal-percentage).
method_decisions.why: Identical either way at the import floor; no case reaches below it.
IEC 60534-2-1 defines the Kv relation with relative density rho1/rho0 and rho0 = 1000 kg/m3 (water at 15 degC rounded); using rho_water(T) instead changes dp by < 0.1 % for 999.1 kg/m3.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A6 pump reverse flow and runout
method_decisions.decision: Same parabola H = H0 s^2 - a q|q| for q < 0 and q > q_runout; warned, not remodelled.
method_decisions.why: Per method.md 5.4. concern: for q < 0 a real centrifugal pump is a turbine/brake quadrant element (Suter curves), not the parabola extrapolated; pump_against_excess_lift numbers are a property of the model, not of a real pump, and a check valve would give q = 0.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A7 velocity head and junction losses
method_decisions.decision: H = h + z; K multiplies the pipe own v^2/2g; no junction or exit losses.
method_decisions.why: Standard hydraulic-grade-line network practice (EPANET, Cross); consistent with fixed nodes being large reservoirs at rest.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A8 demand at a fixed node
method_decisions.decision: Enters only B_n = d_n + out - in.
method_decisions.why: A fixed-pressure node is an infinite source/sink; its demand changes the reported exchange only.

method_decisions.decision: Expected values are converged to machine precision (continuity <= 1e-14 of flow scale). Tolerances are the global rule of the tolerance block, widened per key (case.tolerance_override_abs) to twice the first-order error the page gate (2e-9 scaled residual, h_scale/q_scale of section 6) can leave, computed from |J^-1| of the scaled mixed system at the solution.
method_decisions.why: A reference tighter than what the stopping rule allows would fail a correctly converged page.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A10 zero-flow snap between equal-HGL fixed nodes
method_decisions.decision: q = 0 exactly when dH = 0 across a passive edge.
method_decisions.why: Every passive law is odd with h(0) = 0, so q(0) = 0 is the exact root; the reference inverts q(dH) and gets 0 without a snap. No graded edge has dH = 0.

method_decisions.ambiguity: A11 warnings by name vs id
method_decisions.decision: Expected warnings are listed by edge id, in edge-document order within each kind, kinds in the method.md section 9 order, pump warnings one entry per pump.
method_decisions.why: Names are unique in every case, so the mapping is a bijection.
Per method.md and Swamee & Jain (1976). Colebrook is computed only to record the scatter (crosscheck.swamee_jain_vs_colebrook of the SJ cases).

method_decisions.ambiguity: Refusal message kinds not named in method.md
method_decisions.decision: invalid_json for unparseable text; other kinds as named in method.md section 8.
Every well-posed case (unique root, monotone laws) is expected "solved".
method_decisions.why: All laws are monotone so the root is unique and a damped Newton from any start reaches it; the reference reaches it in < 30 iterations. solved_capped would indicate a solver weakness, not a property of the network.

tolerance.rule: pass if |page - expected| <= max(rel * |expected|, abs) for the key family, or <= case.tolerance_override_abs[key] when that is given (page-gate bound, A9)

flow_*.why: gate 2e-9 on scaled residuals moves flows by O(1e-9) relative in well-conditioned cases; 1e-6 leaves 1000x margin; per-key override where the gate allows more

head_loss_*.why: head-loss error = h'(q) dq, same order as flow error times the law exponent (<= 3)

pump_head_*.why: parabola evaluated at q, error 2 a q dq

head_across_*.why: difference of two HGLs, each bounded by the energy residual gate 2e-9 h_scale

hgl_*.why: 2e-9 h_scale <= 1e-6 m for h_scale up to 500 m

pressure_*.why: rho g/1000 x HGL tolerance (~1e-5 kPa per 1e-6 m)

boundary_*.why: sum of incident flows, continuity gate

Re_*.why: vD/nu, same relative error as flow

f_*.why: df/dRe x dRe is below 1e-6 relative except across the 2000-4000 blend where the override applies

tolerance.outcome, message_kind, notification_kind: exact match (warnings: kinds and component id lists, order as section 9, threshold ties per the section 9 tie rule)
tolerance.monotone: strict ordering of the throttle sequence as stated in the throttle cases
